deck.title: mikedemo.work — a CV that knows its audience

props.title: A CV that ==knows its audience==.
props.subtitle: One master resume, rendered for whoever is reading it — no forks, no stale PDFs.

slides.notes: Hook: everyone reading your CV is different — so why does every reader get the same document? Set up that this site answers that.

left.label: A static resume
left.title: One-size-fits-none
points: Every reader cares about something different
A PDF can't tell partnership wins from product work
It can't tailor itself to the company reading it

right.label: What readers actually want
right.title: Framed for them
points: A hiring manager scans the most relevant track record first
A partner sees the deals, not the sprint cadence
The same true story, angled at the audience

slides.notes: The tension: one document can't serve every reader. Not because the content is wrong — because the framing can't change.

props.title: A ==living CV== with a front door for every reader.

tiles.title: Built from one master resume
tiles.body: The public CV site is generated from a single source of truth.

tiles.title: Personalized landing pages
tiles.body: Share a link with a company slug — that reader lands on a version framed for them.

tiles.title: Live, not attached
tiles.body: Always current, clickable, and addressable at a URL you control.

tiles.title: Playable history
tiles.body: An /adventure/ route turns the career into a text-adventure game.

tiles.title: Open source
tiles.body: The whole thing lives in a public repo.

slides.notes: Walk the grid left to right. The headline capability is the personalization link — everything else hangs off the same master resume.

props.title: One source of truth, ==many front doors==.

items.title: Master resume
items.body: A single master resume holds every role, win, and fact — the only place content is edited.

items.title: Rendered into the public CV
items.body: The CV site is generated from that source, so it can never drift out of date.

items.title: Personalized by the URL
items.body: Per-reader personalization is driven by the link — no forked copies to maintain, ever.

slides.notes: The architecture point: personalization happens at render time from the URL, so there's exactly one copy of the truth.

props.label: The playful side
props.title: Your career, ==as a text adventure==.
props.body: The /adventure/ route turns the career history into something you can play — jobs become rooms, wins become discoveries. A CV someone remembers, because they played it.

slides.notes: Personality beat. If the room smiles, say: it's the same resume content — just rendered as an adventure instead of a PDF.
